findings.message: The load envelope is redirect-centric only (100 redirects/sec, 20 concurrent visitors/link, 10^6 corpus). The shorten/write path carries no capacity bound: no submissions-per-second ceiling and no max link-creation rate are named or deferred. This matters because BRD.01.11.341c couples each shorten to a synchronous external reputation-source call, so the write path's load profile drives the dependency's sizing and fail-closed-rejection rate — yet that profile is unconstrained, leaving the write path's resilience posture undefined at business altitude.
findings.recommendation: Declare a business-altitude write-path capacity bound (e.g. peak shorten requests/sec and/or max new links/day) alongside the existing redirect envelope in §9, or explicitly defer it to a named ADR slot. Tie the bound to the reputation-source dependency so its fail-closed behaviour can be sized.

findings.message: §9 names a target link corpus on the order of 10^6 links, but no capacity-exhaustion response is declared for storage-corpus saturation. The §12 BRD.01.12.8b9b response addresses short-code-space depletion, which is distinct from running out of link-record storage capacity. When the corpus bound is approached the business behaviour (alert ops / reject new creates / degrade) is unstated.
findings.recommendation: Add a corpus-saturation response to §9 or §12 mirroring the short-code-exhaustion pattern (utilization alert threshold, then reject-new-creates-with-clear-error while existing links stay resolvable), or explicitly state the corpus figure is a sizing target with response deferred to a named ADR slot.

findings.message: §9 declares throughput beyond the 100 redirects/sec envelope 'out of scope' but names no overload response when legitimate traffic exceeds it (a benign client retry storm or a viral link). With no shed/reject/degrade stance, behaviour above the envelope is silently undefined against the ≥99.9% availability and p95<50ms commitments — a cascade or latency-blowout under accidental legitimate load has no declared business stance.
findings.recommendation: Add a business-altitude over-envelope stance to §9 (e.g. when redirect load exceeds the envelope the business accepts shedding/queuing excess with the latency target suspended for the overage while existing-link resolvability is preserved), or explicitly defer the overload-response decision to the Redirect Performance ADR topic (BRD.01.08.66e2).
